note: The documents a venture makes (EE-218). A record is the source of truth; a document is an artifact rendered from records and never the record. The catalog is opinionated on purpose: the formats say what each one is for, the rules say when slides beat a printed document, the ladder says a printable reading copy a person approved comes before any interactive page and the page before the live site, and each kind names the records its sections read, so every claim in a rendered document cites a record. Checked by packages/naive/src/checks/check-documents.ts; rendered by packages/naive/src/engine/render-document.ts.

formats.name: Markdown
formats.reads: alone and in order, on a screen or in a terminal
formats.why: The reading copy every document starts as: plain text a person reads end to end, that diffs in git and that Naive renders in house with no dependency.

formats.name: PDF
formats.reads: alone and in order, on paper or on a screen, laid out the same everywhere
formats.why: The reading copy a person prints and carries into a meeting, or sends to someone who must not change it.

formats.name: Word document
formats.reads: alone and in order, with the reader editing as they go
formats.why: Only when the reader must edit the words or the file goes into someone else's process, such as counsel marking up terms.

formats.name: Slide deck
formats.reads: in a room, with a person speaking over it
formats.why: A live talk, where the speaker carries the argument and each slide holds one point. Never a document with the words made smaller.

formats.name: Interactive page
formats.reads: on a screen, in whatever order the reader clicks
formats.why: Only once the reading copy is approved: a page a person can click through, to try the layout and the interaction before anything is built.

formats.name: Live site
formats.why: The published site. It is a one-way door in public, so it comes last and through the publishing gate (EE-025).

rules.when: Nothing has been written down yet and the work is about what the document says
rules.why: Words are the thing being decided. A page or a deck hides a weak argument behind layout, and a person cannot mark up a layout.

rules.when: A person will read it before or during a meeting, alone and in order
rules.why: A reader sets their own pace and goes back a paragraph. Slides read alone lose the speaker, which is most of their content.

rules.when: A person will speak over it to an audience, and the audience cannot read and listen at once
rules.why: The speaker carries the argument; the slide holds the one point the room should be looking at while they say it.
Write the narrative as a reading copy first and have a person approve it. A deck built before the argument is settled is design work done twice.

rules.when: The reader must change the words, or their own process needs the file
rules.why: The only reason to leave Markdown and PDF. Counsel marking up terms is the usual case.

rules.when: The question is how a person moves through it, not what it says, and the reading copy is approved
rules.why: Clicking is the only way to answer a question about clicking. Until then an interactive page is a slower way to review prose.

rules.when: People outside the venture will find it
rules.why: Published words cannot be unpublished. The publishing gate and a person's approval come before the deploy, never after.

ladder.note: Fail closed. A rung is built only once the rung it comes after exists as a live artifact a person approved, which is the ladder's own requirement and is why no rung repeats it under requires. The founder's rule: build the printable reading copy first, read it, approve it, and only then let anyone open an editor.

rungs.what: A printable copy a person reads end to end and could hand round a table
Slides for a live talk, one point a slide, built from the approved narrative
A page a person clicks through, to settle layout and interaction before anything is built
The published site, through the publishing gate

kinds.title: One-pager
kinds.purpose: Let someone who has never heard of the venture say what it is, who it is for and why now, after one page
kinds.why_format: It is read alone, and printed for a meeting, so it is a document and never slides.

kinds.title: Decision memo
kinds.purpose: Put one open question, its live ideas and the evidence behind each in front of the person who decides
kinds.why_format: A reader weighs ideas against each other, going back and forth. Slides force one order and hide the comparison.

sections.title: What the venture has already committed to

kinds.title: Work brief
kinds.purpose: Let whoever picks up a handoff start without asking anything first
kinds.why_format: It is read on a screen beside the work and changes as the work moves, so it stays Markdown and is never printed or laid out.

kinds.title: Meeting pack
kinds.purpose: Let everyone at a meeting arrive having read the same thing, so the meeting is spent deciding
kinds.why_format: It is printed and read before the meeting, in order, by people who will not all be in the room when it is explained.

sections.title: The promise we are held to

kinds.title: Board and investor update
kinds.purpose: Tell the people who backed the venture what moved, what did not, and what is being asked of them
kinds.why_format: It is read alone, kept, and often forwarded, so the layout must not change under the reader. That is a PDF, not a deck and not a live page.

kinds.title: Pitch deck
kinds.purpose: Carry one argument for the venture through a meeting a person is speaking in
kinds.why_format: Slides because a person speaks over it, and a reading copy first because the argument is settled in words, not in layout. The PDF is the handout, not the talk.

kinds.title: Product spec
kinds.purpose: Say what a product does and does not do, closely enough that someone can build it and someone else can check it
kinds.why_format: It lives beside the code, is read in parts and changes often, so it stays Markdown in the repository.

sections.title: The principles it is held to

kinds.title: Site copy
kinds.purpose: Settle what the site says to a stranger, in the order they will read it, before anyone builds a page
kinds.why_format: The only kind that climbs the whole ladder: the words as a reading copy a person approves, then one page to click through, then the live site through the publishing gate.

sections.title: The first thing a stranger reads
What they are trying to do

kinds.title: Architecture decision record
kinds.purpose: Let someone who joins later see one architecture decision: the question, the options weighed, what was decided and why
kinds.why_format: It lives in the repository beside the code it decides, is read on a screen and kept with the code's history, so it stays Markdown and is never laid out.

sections.title: Consequences
sections.hole: What becomes easier or harder because of this decision. No record type holds consequences yet: a decision record's outcomes say what it is expected to achieve, not what it costs.

kinds.title: Release note
kinds.purpose: Tell the people who use the product what it does now and what changed in this release, in their words
kinds.why_format: It is read once, on a screen, where the product is, and kept beside the release, so it stays Markdown; putting it on the site is the site's own ladder.

sections.title: The release
sections.hole: The release's version and date. No record type holds a release yet: the release card under .release/ has no schema.

sections.title: What is new and what was fixed
sections.hole: Which capabilities and bugs belong to this release. A bug's fixed_in names a version, and no record says which version this release is, so they cannot be picked out yet.

kinds.title: Changelog entry
kinds.purpose: Record what changed in one version for the people who build on it, grouped as added, changed and fixed
kinds.why_format: A changelog is one Markdown file in the repository, newest version first, read in a terminal or on the forge, so it is never laid out.

sections.title: Version
sections.hole: The release's version and date. No record type holds a release yet: the release card under .release/ has no schema.

sections.title: Added, changed and fixed
sections.hole: Which capabilities were added or changed and which bugs were fixed in this version. That needs a release record, which no record type holds yet.

kinds.title: Requirements specification
kinds.purpose: Say what the venture requires, which goal each requirement serves and how each is verified, closely enough that someone can build to it and someone else can check it
kinds.why_format: It is read in parts beside the work and changes as requirements settle, so it stays Markdown in the repository.
